messages.content: I have a restaurant visit in Pittsburgh on Monday, September 15, currently blocked for 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. See whether I can do it from Chicago in one day. Do not book anything yet because they still owe me a final start time.
What is the restaurant location, and are you leaving from home or already near O'Hare? Those two details will determine whether the first nonstop leaves enough margin.
It is in Monroeville, near the turnpike. I would leave from home in Lincoln Square.

For a same-day trip, the workable outbound is a 6:05 a.m. nonstop from O'Hare arriving Pittsburgh at 8:29 a.m. Eastern. Business is currently $486 round trip; coach is $318. With a 35-minute drive to O'Hare at that hour, parking, and security, you would need to leave home around 4:15 a.m. A rental car pickup would put you on the road around 9:05, and normal Monday traffic to Monroeville is about 30 to 40 minutes. That gives an estimated arrival of 9:35 to 9:45, so the margin for a 10:00 start is thin but real.
What happens if the flight is even a little late?

A 20-minute delay likely puts you at the restaurant around 10:00. A 30-minute delay makes you late. Rideshare would save roughly 10 to 15 minutes over collecting a rental, but it would leave you dependent on a return pickup after the visit. The current one-way rideshare estimate is $58 to $74 each way.
Use rideshare for the same-day comparison. I will not need a car during the visit. What is the latest sensible flight home?

The best return nonstop leaves Pittsburgh at 6:20 p.m. and reaches O'Hare at 7:04 p.m. Central. Leaving the restaurant at 3:15 allows about 45 minutes to the airport in afternoon traffic, plus just over two hours for security and any traffic variance. There is also a 5:05 p.m. nonstop, but that compresses the drive and airport time too much after a 3:00 finish.
Keep the 6:20. Compare the full same-day cost against flying Sunday night and staying over.

Same day is $486 in business, about $132 for the midpoint rideshare estimate, and roughly $42 for O'Hare parking, for a working total of $660. Coach would reduce that to $492. The Sunday fallback uses a 6:35 p.m. nonstop arriving at 9:02 p.m. Business paired with the same Monday return is $524. A well-reviewed hotel in Monroeville is $154 including tax, airport-to-hotel rideshare is about $68, hotel-to-restaurant and restaurant-to-airport together are about $91, and O'Hare parking rises to about $63. Working total: $900 in business or $721 in coach.
I would rather take business when the difference is reasonable. Keep business in front for both structures, but coach can stay as the fallback.

Understood. The Sunday option costs about $240 more in business but removes the morning flight risk and the 4:15 a.m. departure from home. It also gets you near the restaurant the night before. The same-day option is financially cleaner, but I would only use it if the restaurant confirms that 10:00 is firm or can tolerate a short delay.
Could Sunday night be cheaper if I stay near the airport instead?

Slightly. An airport hotel is $126 including tax, with a free shuttle from the terminal. Rideshare to Monroeville Monday morning is about $69, and the afternoon ride back is about $70. Including the $524 business fare and $63 O'Hare parking, that version totals about $852. It saves $48 versus sleeping in Monroeville, but adds a 35- to 50-minute drive before the visit.

Carry forward the same-day business pair and the Sunday airport-hotel version. I want the lodging and exact total side by side after they confirm whether the visit really starts at 10:00. No booking before that.

I will hold the comparison at two unbooked structures: same day on the 6:05 a.m. outbound and 6:20 p.m. return, estimated at $660 with rideshares and parking; or Sunday night on the 6:35 p.m. outbound with the same Monday return and an airport hotel, estimated at $852. Business is the lead cabin and coach remains available if needed. The key decision point is the confirmed restaurant start time; nothing has been purchased or reserved.
